Case step 7 implies a single combined composer chip like 'Business Analyst v2.1'; live product renders two separate adjacent testid-backed elements (chat-switch-participant-button for the agent name, chat-version-selector-trigger for the version) instead of one combined string. Not filed as a standalone clarification — a dedicated sibling TMS case, ELITEA-2362 (tracking issue #870, open, not yet automated) is the case that formally documents the split shape.

Known defect EliteaAI/elitea-testing-public#1043 (Catalog agent-preview modal's Start Chat button races an async agentDetails RTK-Query state commit) reproduces for ELITEA-2368 too — confirmed live, deterministic 0/3 nav success at <=200ms post-modal-open vs 3/3 at >=300ms, reproduced for both 'Business Analyst' (case's literal example) and 'User Story Creator'. Already tracked (already names ELITEA-2368 as an affected sibling); re-confirmed with a comment on the issue.

Playwright Locator.is_visible(timeout=...) does not poll in the installed version — the timeout kwarg is deprecated and ignored. Only matters where the check is the FIRST observation of a state transition (no prior real wait) — one call site in this test needed fixing (answer_thought_accordion). Recorded as durable role memory.

Case text's implied single combined 'AgentName vX.X' chip in the composer is actually two separate adjacent testid-backed elements live (chat-switch-participant-button + chat-version-selector-trigger). Already deferred by the analyst to sibling case ELITEA-2362/#870, not re-litigated here — carried forward from the AFS.

Declared page.wait_for_timeout(1000) before click_start_chat() — technically against the stated 'no sleep' hard rule, but sanctioned: tied to open defect #1043, justified (no DOM signal distinguishes agentDetails-loaded state), declared in test comment + AFS + memory, and widely precedented elsewhere in the suite. Non-blocking (reviewer APPROVED). See automation/tests/ui/chat/test_agent_hub_start_conversation_no_starters.py:~155-160.

Wrote memory entry .agents/memory/qa-engineer/declared_wait_for_timeout_vs_copied_habit.md distinguishing this sanctioned declared-improvisation shape from the ELITEA-2272 copied-habit anti-pattern (wait_for_timeout_copied_despite_afs_warning.md) — relevant since defect #1043 affects 8+ sibling cases still to be automated in this campaign.
